_comment: Facts a correct handling of this call has to reach the caller. End-state
checking cannot see any of them: the card ends up active with the review
lifted, the hold approved and a travel note on file whether or not the agent
warned that the line only stretches so far or that the note guarantees
nothing. He is standing at a hotel desk about to have the card run again, so
what he is told is what determines whether the next attempt works.
Each entry is satisfied when any one of its surface forms appears in the
agent's utterances, matched case-insensitively with whitespace collapsed.
A form that is a single number or a single word is matched on boundaries; a
form of two or more words is matched as a plain substring. That is why bare
figures like '15' are listed: '15' will find "15 USD", "15.00 dollars" and
"a total of 15", but will not match '$150', so an agent that quotes the wrong
amount gets no credit. Bare words are fenced for the same reason - 'two' must
not be found inside 'network'. Anchors are only ever the whole value: 'five'
is not listed for 95, since "five business days" would then satisfy a fee.
The alternatives exist so an agent is not failed for saying 'nine hundred and
twelve dollars' instead of '$912'. Every form is a distinctive multi-word
phrase or a specific figure; nothing here would match an arbitrary
transcript.
Requirements already asserted against the database are deliberately not
repeated: the review being lifted, the card returning to active, the hold
being re-presented, the resulting available credit and the travel notice
existing are all checked as state.

required.why: everything else in this call turns on the size of the line; he is about to authorise a hotel stay and cannot judge whether the next attempt will clear without knowing what is actually available
any_of: 912 dollars
912 dollar
nine hundred and twelve dollars
nine hundred twelve dollars

required.why: he is about to tell the front desk to run 840 again, and hotels routinely authorise above the room rate for incidentals; without that warning he thinks the number he was quoted is the number that gets charged
any_of: more than the room total
more than the total room charge
more than the room rate
above the room total
above the room rate
more than the cost of the room
more than just the room
on top of the room rate
on top of the room total
extra for incidentals
hold for incidentals on top

required.why: the whole authorisation has to be covered by the remaining line or it fails outright; this is the rule that decides whether his next attempt goes through, and it is the one thing he can act on by asking the desk what they are about to run

a larger hold might not
a bigger hold may not

required.why: he is being handed a lifted block and a travel note and will reasonably read both as a promise that the card now works; neither guarantees any particular purchase is approved, and saying so is the one honest limit available in this call
any_of: does not guarantee every purchase
doesn't guarantee every purchase

does not guarantee approval
doesn't guarantee approval

isn't a guarantee of approval
no guarantee every purchase will be approved
cannot guarantee every transaction
can't guarantee every transaction
cannot promise every purchase will go through

does not guarantee the card will be approved

required.why: the 840 hold will sit against his line for days after he leaves, and he is travelling; if he assumes it clears at checkout he will plan spending he does not have
